FINDING_ID: LB_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.96  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._solve_greedy()` does not optimise the objective it claims to solve. It ranks candidates only by current load fraction and never consults `_objective()`, so it can return a much worse feasible allocation than one already available. I verified this with two equal-capacity PAR models where one cost `100x` more: the greedy split produced objective `1013.0002`, while assigning both tasks to the cheap model was feasible and scored `26.0009`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rank each candidate placement by incremental objective increase `ΔJ` instead of raw load fraction, or use the current greedy pass only as a seed and then run local improvement / ILP for small instances.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.97  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: `_solve_greedy()` intentionally violates HARD feasibility `F1` by force-assigning a task when no model can fit it, and `solve()` still returns that allocation instead of failing. That breaks the stated contract of a constrained allocator. I verified this with a task of size `80` against admissible models with `L=50`: `dispatch_check()` correctly returned `False`, but `solve()` still returned an allocation overloading the model and only emitted a warning.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Never force an `F1` violation. Return an explicit infeasible result or raise a typed exception so the caller can decompose the task, relax redundancy, or skip dispatch.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: `_redundancy_target()` uses `len(self.models)` instead of the number of admissible executors. When `K > 1`, PM is excluded by `_admissibility_mask()`, so critical tasks can demand redundancy that is mathematically unreachable. I verified this with `PM + 2 PAR`: a critical task got target `3` while only `2` models were admissible, producing unavoidable degraded-allocation warnings and under-coverage.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute redundancy against the admissible active set for that task, for example `sum(admissibility[j])`, and clamp the target to that count before allocation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `_objective()` and `_balanced()` include the idle PM in load-fraction variance and bottleneck calculations even though PM is intentionally inadmissible for normal work. That makes a perfectly even worker split look unbalanced. I verified this with `PM + 2 PAR` and a 50/50 split across the two PAR workers: worker variance was `0.0`, but the code measured variance over `[0.0, 0.5, 0.5]` and reported `balanced=False`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute latency and balance terms only over models admissible for the current task set, or at minimum exclude fixed-idle PM capacity from those statistics.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: The probabilistic feasibility extension is not wired into the actual allocation path. `feasibility_probability()` and `dispatch_check()` exist, but neither `LoadBalancer.solve()` nor `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` uses them. I verified this with a model `L=100, L_std=30` and a `95`-token task: `dispatch_check()` returned `(False, 0.566...)`, yet both the load balancer and manager still allocated the task to that model.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Apply the feasibility threshold during candidate selection inside `solve()`/`get_allocation()`, using cumulative planned load rather than exposing the check as an optional side call.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86  
DESCRIPTION: The adaptive-routing and capability-selection story is disconnected from task allocation. `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` says work is matched to live demonstrated capability, but `LoadBalancer` ignores `ModelSpec.fingerprint` and `Task.flaw_class` entirely. I verified this by swapping a very strong and very weak PAR model while keeping `L`, `c`, and `tau` identical: the allocation matrix was unchanged. So live fingerprint updates currently affect role reassignment, not load balancing.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a task-to-model utility term based on live fingerprints and task type, then use that term in candidate ranking or the main objective so allocation actually changes when capability estimates change.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
